paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is the One who lifts people up and brings people down. The song says it plainly: "exaltation comes neither from east nor west, nor out of the desert, but it is God who judges; He brings down one and exalts another" (Psalm 75:6-7). So the promotion, the spotlight and the corner office are not handed out by whoever looks the strongest. That's good news if you've ever felt stuck at the back of a drawer, and I have, so I'm allowed to say it.

Now look at who gets warned. The voice tells the proud, "Do not boast," and tells the wicked not to lift up their horn against heaven (Psalm 75:4-5). Strutting with your neck stretched out doesn't work when somebody else holds the cup (Psalm 75:8). I think that's a gentle push for all of us to check our own necks, because mine has been out there before, and my chef's hat paid for it.

And here's where the song lands, so rest in it. God says He will judge fairly when He chooses the time (Psalm 75:2), and He says "the horns of the righteous will be exalted" (Psalm 75:10). The singer's answer is to give thanks and keep singing: "I will proclaim Him forever" (Psalm 75:9). So bake your batch, do right, and let God handle the lifting, baker. He's way better at it than the east, the west or the desert.
